llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a severe fibre-loss event, effectively a cable cut or crushed/damaged fibre, in the S14-adjacent segment of the S14–S04 route. The coincident OSC loss on both directional representations of that physical segment, downstream amplifier input LOS, and broad channel loss strongly localize it there; unchanged amplifier pump/current telemetry argues against an amplifier failure.

proposals.rationale: OSC_LOS at oms.S14-S04.span0 (O126) and input LOS at the next amplifier (O1) directly indicate severe loss in the first span leaving S14. The matching reverse-fibre loss at E14 suggests damage to the common physical cable segment; the only concern is that alarms on S14–S20 imply the damage may extend across a larger cable corridor.

O125 and the receiving preamp LOS O123 localize severe loss to the final S04-to-S14 span, which is the reverse fibre paired with E23. It explains loss in that direction, though E23 is the clearer localization from the first downstream amplifier alarm.

A disconnected OMS input patch at S14 could remove all outgoing channels toward S04 abruptly. It does not adequately explain OSC loss on the reverse fibre or the simultaneous S14–S20 span alarms, and there was no recent S14 maintenance.

A ROADM WSS port failure at S14 could interrupt many channels and account for the concentration of affected services at S14. However, a WSS failure should not lose the OSC on adjacent spans, so the physical-span evidence strongly argues against it.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: Failure of the S14-to-S04 booster could remove all downstream traffic. Its input/output power and pump-current instruments saw no change, and a booster failure would not normally cause OSC loss, making this unlikely.
